bib.title: News Summarization and Evaluation in the Era of GPT-3

read.skipped: References skimmed only; annotator instruction screenshots (Figs 14-15) have no text.

question: How do prompted GPT-3 news summaries compare with fine-tuned summarizers in human preference, and can existing automatic metrics evaluate them?
contributions: First systematic study of prompt-based GPT-3 vs fine-tuned models for news summarization (human A/B study)
Evidence that reference-based and reference-free automatic metrics fail on GPT-3 summaries
Study of keyword- and aspect-based summarization with prompting
Release of 10K generated summaries over 4 benchmarks and 1K human preference judgments

method.summary: A/B crowd study on 100 recent CNN and 100 recent BBC articles comparing zero-shot text-davinci-002, BRIO and T0, then scoring 500-article samples from four benchmarks with reference-based and reference-free metrics, plus a keyword-focused A/B study against CTRLSum.

datasets.name: CNN/DM, XSum, Newsroom test splits
datasets.size: 500 random articles per dataset (CNN, DailyMail, XSum, Newsroom)

inference.decoding: GPT3-D2: not stated; BRIO-XSum: beam size 10, fallback to lower beam candidate or drop first article sentence and resample
inference.samples: one summary per article per system (inferred: no repeated sampling is described)
inference.prompting: zero-shot; 'Article: {{article}}\nSummarize the above article in N sentences.' N=3 CNN/DailyMail, 2 Newsroom, 1 XSum/BBC

other.T0 prompts: CNN/DM 'Summarize the article below in 3 to 4 sentences?'; Newsroom 2 to 3; XSum 1 sentence
other.api_cost: about 2600 GPT3-D2 summaries, about $150, $0.06 per 1K tokens

metrics.name: Best/worst preference (majority vote)
metrics.definition: percentage of articles where a system is chosen best or worst by majority of 3 annotators; ties allowed

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L, METEOR, BLEU, BERTScore, MoverScore, QAEval EM/F1
SUPERT, BLANC, QuestEval, QAFactEval, FactCC, DAE, SummaC
metrics.definition: reference-free; entailment models scored with P(factual | article, summary)

eval.protocol: Prolific crowd annotators: 60 per dataset, 5 articles each, 3 annotators per article, US residents for CNN and UK for BBC, about $11/hr ($4 per task); no quality definition given; multiple selections allowed; paired bootstrap significance test.

prompts.text:
Article: {{article}}
Summarize the above article in N sentences.
Summarize the above article briefly in 1 sentence.
Summarize the above article in 2-3 sentences focusing on William Barr.
Summarize the article below in 3 to 4 sentences?

results.claim: Annotators preferred zero-shot GPT3-D2 as best on CNN-style summaries.
results.setup: 100 CNN-2022 articles, majority vote of 3 Prolific annotators, GPT3-D2 N=3 vs BRIO vs T0
results.table: Table 3, row CNN, column GPT3 Best

results.claim: Annotators preferred GPT3-D2 as best on BBC-style summaries.
results.table: Table 3, row BBC, column GPT3 Best

results.claim: GPT3-D2 beat the next best system by at least 20 points, significant by paired bootstrap.
results.quote: outperforms the next best model by at least 20 percentage points

results.claim: Reference-based metrics ranked GPT3-D2 below BRIO by more than 7 ROUGE-L points, reversing human preference.
results.setup: 500 random test articles per dataset; Table 4

results.table: Table 4, rows CNN BRIO and GPT3-D2, ROUGE-L 31.44 and 24.71
Table 4, rows XSum BRIO and GPT3-D2, ROUGE-L 41.04 and 20.60

results.claim: GPT3-D2 scores fall below the Lead-3 baseline reported in prior work.
results.setup: Fabbri 2021; Grusky 2018 numbers, not re-measured here
results.quote: are even lower than the triv
results.note: Lead-3 figure reported from other work, no number given

results.claim: Unanimous best-summary agreement for GPT3-D2 occurs for under 30% of articles.
results.quote: for less that 30% of the annotated articles

results.claim: Krippendorff alpha agreement is low (0.05 to 0.18 across the four best/worst panels).
results.setup: Fig 5 panels CNN/BBC best/worst, MASI distance
results.note: other panels 0.11, 0.18, 0.15; panel-to-condition mapping not recoverable from text

results.claim: Annotators preferred GPT3-D2 over CTRLSum for keyword-focused summaries.
results.setup: 100 CNN articles, 2 named entities each, 60 annotators, 3 per article

results.claim: Summary length barely explains the preference.
results.setup: GPT3-D2 vs next best, Pearson correlation of length difference and vote difference
results.quote: Pearson’s ρ is 0.17 for CNN and .02

results.claim: GPT3-D2 followed the sentence-count constraint in nearly all instances.

limits: Human study uses overall-quality A/B choice with no quality definition; no dimension-level analysis (authors concede).
English news only; domain-specific fine-tuned models may win in niche domains.
GPT3-D2 training data unknown, may include summarization preference data from RLHF.
Human study only 100 articles per style; only CNN for generic news study, DailyMail excluded; 500-article samples for metrics.
Aspect-based results qualitative and mixed; long-document summarization shown for one example only.

QAEval, QuestEval, QAFactEval, FactCC, DAE, SummaC, SUPERT, BLANC
